description: Comprehensive verification across all 21 screens: visual regression testing, functional testing, performance optimization checks, cross-browser testing (at least Chrome + Firefox), and final documentation. Confirm all acceptance criteria met, no regressions introduced, and application is production-ready.
steps: Read context.json and all previous FEAT findings to understand full scope of changes

Visual Regression Testing: Run 'npm run build' then 'npm run preview' to test production build, manually visit all 21 screens in order (list below), verify each screen loads without errors, animations play smoothly at 60fps, no console errors or warnings, network tab shows reasonable bundle size, record any visual issues in findings

Functional Testing Matrix: For each of 21 screens test: (1) Page loads correctly, (2) API data displays (no mock data), (3) Animations play on entrance, (4) Hover effects work, (5) Click actions execute, (6) Modals/drawers open smoothly, (7) Forms submit successfully if present, (8) Empty states show when appropriate, (9) Skeletons display during loading, (10) Mobile responsive at 375px, record pass/fail for each screen in findings

21 Screens to Test: Creator Dashboard, New Content, My Submissions, AI Review, Creator Guidelines, Exception Requests, Sentinel Tasks, Notifications, Approved Content, Profile | Manager Overview, Review Queue, All Submissions, Brand Guidelines, Rules & Conflicts, Exceptions, Rule Impact Sandbox, Sentinel Monitoring, Asset Library, Analytics & Health, Audit History

Performance Optimization: Run 'npm run build' and inspect dist/ folder size (target <500KB gzipped for main JS bundle), run Chrome DevTools Lighthouse audit on 3 representative screens (Creator Dashboard, AI Review, Manager Overview) and record Performance scores (target >85), use Performance profiler to record 5-second interaction on AI Review screen and verify 60fps frame rate, check for memory leaks by navigating between 5 screens and observing memory in DevTools (should not grow unbounded), record performance metrics in findings

Cross-Browser Testing: Test on Chrome (primary browser), test on at least one other browser (Firefox preferred, Edge acceptable), focus on animation smoothness, layout consistency, font rendering, record any browser-specific issues in findings

Final Verification Checklist: All 21 screens load without errors ✓, All animations play smoothly ✓, No console errors ✓, API data displays correctly ✓, Mobile responsive ✓, Accessibility passes (prefers-reduced-motion, keyboard nav) ✓, Performance acceptable ✓, Cross-browser consistent ✓

Documentation: Update or create docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md documenting color usage, typography, animation timing standards, component library (list all motion components with props), capture 5-10 representative screenshots at 1920x1080 resolution and save to docs/screenshots/ (at minimum: Creator Dashboard, AI Review, New Content, Manager Overview, Review Queue), optionally update PRECEDENT_UI_DESIGN_AUDIT.md with 'After' state summary
Record comprehensive findings: any issues discovered during testing, any edge cases to watch, performance metrics, browser compatibility notes, final summary of transformation
acceptance_criteria: Lighthouse Performance score >85 on tested screens
Works consistently on Chrome and at least one other browser
verification: Run 'npm run preview' and manually test all 21 screens systematically
Run Chrome DevTools Lighthouse on 3 screens, verify scores
Record interactions in Performance profiler, verify 60fps
Test on second browser (Firefox or Edge)
Capture screenshots and save to docs/screenshots/
Review findings document to confirm all issues addressed
Final check: npm run typecheck passes, npm run build succeeds, preview works flawlessly
Expected: Production-ready application with world-class UI across all 21 screens
findings: HARNESS: added scripts/verify_21_screens.mjs, which logs in as both roles against the running dev server (127.0.0.1:5173, backend :8000), walks every screen, records console errors, page errors, failed requests, horizontal overflow and h1 count, and writes 1920x1080 screenshots. 27 visits total: 11 manager screens at 1920x1080 with screenshots, 4 manager screens repeated at 375px, 10 creator screens at 1920x1080 with screenshots, and 2 creator screens under an emulated prefers-reduced-motion context. RESULTS: 25 of 27 visits completely clean; every visit rendered exactly one h1; zero horizontal overflow at both 1920px and 375px. The 2 non-clean visits are both AI Review and both carry a single console error from the same source: GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/analysis/{id}/file returns 404 because the currently selected submission has no stored analysis file. The view handles this (the fetch is caught and the panel renders 'No poster attached'), so it is a handled, pre-existing API 404 rather than a UI regression, but it does surface in the browser console and would be worth silencing at the API layer. Slowest navigations (cold dev server, networkidle wait, not production numbers): review-queue 2715ms, asset-library 2585ms, all-submissions 2563ms. BUNDLE: production build is 1,188.81 kB raw / 318.51 kB gzip for the main JS chunk and 173.81 kB raw / 28.13 kB gzip for CSS — inside the 500 kB gzip target. DOCS: created docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md (palette table, type scale, motion principles, every motion component with its props, tone enum, patterns) and docs/screenshots/ with 21 full-resolution screenshots covering all screens. NOT VERIFIED, stated plainly rather than claimed: (1) Lighthouse was not run — no Lighthouse/DevTools automation is available in this environment, so the '>85 Performance score' criterion is unverified; (2) 60fps was not profiled with a performance trace, although every animation in the system animates only transform/opacity, which is what keeps it on the compositor; (3) cross-browser testing was not performed — only Chromium is installed here, so Firefox and Edge are untested; (4) no memory-leak soak test was run. These four remain open items for a machine with DevTools/browser access. FUNCTIONAL SPOT CHECKS observed during the run: API data rendered on every screen (no mock data paths), skeletons resolved into content, filters/tabs rendered, drawers and modals opened from the queue and library screens, and the reduced-motion pass rendered static final states with no errors.
